scorecards.inningsCommentary: Australia commenced their first innings at Sydney Cricket Ground, aiming to set an imposing baseline total. The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 215 from M Labuschagne, complemented by a commanding 156-run stand between Steve Smith and M Labuschagne that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 3.02 RPO. New Zealand's bowling response was spearheaded by Neil Wagner (3/66), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Finishing at 454/10 (150.1 ov), Australia established an overwhelming first-innings foundation that firmly dictated the terms of the match.

The centerpiece of the innings was a brilliant 52 from Colin Grandhomme, complemented by a commanding 69-run stand between Colin Grandhomme and BJ Watling that absorbed bowling hostility and accelerated the scoring rate to 2.84 RPO. Australia's bowling response was spearheaded by Nathan Lyon (5/50), who generated sustained pressure and triggered critical breakthroughs to prevent runaway scoring. Dismissed for 136/9 (47.5 ov), New Zealand succumbed to fourth-innings pressure as Australia's bowlers closed out the victory.

Nathan Lyon spearheaded Australia's attack to bowl out New Zealand for 136/9 and seal victory.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Sydney Cricket Ground commenced with high tactical intensity as Australia posted 454/10 (150.1 ov) in their opening innings. In response, New Zealand countered with 251/10 (95.4 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during Century: M Labuschagne 215 (363b), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, M Labuschagne delivered a masterclass for Australia (274 Runs & 1 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Australia 57%) and allowing Australia to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, New Zealand faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Australia's bowling unit, bolstered by Nathan Lyon (6 Runs & 10 Wkts), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Australia won by 279 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Australia's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While New Zealand produced fighting phases, Australia won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
